description: Core data models, abstractions, and data-source logic for KumikoUI DataGrid. Platform-independent — no rendering or UI framework references.
releaseNotes:
First 1.0 prerelease. All four packages (KumikoUI.Core, KumikoUI.SkiaSharp, KumikoUI.Maui, KumikoUI.Uno) ship at this version, and each package depends on the exact version of its siblings. The API may still change before 1.0.0. KumikoUI.Uno is the least verified host. The release brings the 1.0 API review and `sealed`/value-type changes (#37, #112), `KumikoSource` thread affinity (#69), saved layouts, column reordering and context menus (#98, #100), native text input on iOS, Android, Windows and Uno (#40-#43), and the hardware-accelerated render mode on MAUI (`KumikoRenderMode.Hardware`, #71); the entries marked **Breaking:** below list what to change when upgrading from 0.2.0. See [docs/release/1.0.0-preview.1-release-notes.md](https://github.com/TheEightBot/KumikoUI/blob/v1.0.0-preview.1/docs/release/1.0.0-preview.1-release-notes.md) for the summary and known issues.

### Added
- Sample apps (#97): a Styling page (image column, icon sets, `CellStyleResolver` and `RowStyleResolver`, `AlternateRowBackground`) and an Events page (event log for `CellTapped`, `HeaderTapped`, `ContextMenuRequested`, `RowDoubleTapped`, `CellValueChanged`, `ValidationFailed` and `SelectionChanged`, the selection modes, `CellValidator`, `KumikoLayoutState` save and restore) on both samples, `samples/README.md` with per-head run commands and a feature-to-page map. The MAUI Android activity uses `AdjustResize` and the Uno one now does too (it was `AdjustNothing`, which left the keyboard over the edited cell); the MAUI sample uses `DisplayAlertAsync`, creates its commands once, and both samples ignore a second request to open a dialog, modal page or the initial page while one is open. The MAUI pages' toolbars are one horizontally scrolling row, so a phone keeps its room above the keyboard for the grid.
- `ScrollState.BottomInset` (extra scrollable room below the content, included in `MaxOffsetY`) and `KumikoKeyboardAvoidance` (`KumikoUI.Core.Layout`: `GetObscuredHeight`, `GetScrollDelta`, `ScrollEditorIntoView`), the keyboard geometry the hosts share (#258).
- `KumikoStyle.CheckBoxBorderColor`: the outline color of a Boolean cell's check box. `null` (the default) keeps drawing it in `GridLineColor`; set it when soft grid lines leave an unchecked box hard to see.
- `UnoActionButtonDefinition` (`KumikoUI.Uno`): a `DependencyObject` implementation of `IActionButtonDefinition` with `Label`, `BackgroundColor`, `TextColor`, `Command` and `CommandParameter` as dependency properties, so action buttons can be declared and bound in Uno XAML like `MauiActionButtonDefinition` on MAUI (#64). `KumikoDataGrid` gives the definitions of its `ActionButtonsCellRenderer` columns its `DataContext`, so `{Binding ViewDetailsCommand}` resolves against the page's view model, and redraws when a definition changes. The Uno MVVM sample page declares its columns and buttons in XAML.
- Background view rebuilds (#254): `BackgroundRebuildThreshold` on the MAUI (bindable) and Uno (dependency property) grids, forwarded to the data source (default 10,000), and `KumikoSource.BackgroundRebuildThreshold`, `KumikoSource.DefaultBackgroundRebuildThreshold` (10 000), `IsViewUpdatePending`, the `ViewUpdated` event and `WhenViewUpdatedAsync()`. From the threshold up, sorting, filtering, grouping and summaries are rebuilt on a worker from a copy of the items and settings; requests made in one UI turn (including `PropertyChanged` of a sorted, filtered or grouped property) start one rebuild, a newer request cancels a running one, and the finished view is swapped in on the UI thread, raising `ViewChanged` (`Rebuild`) then `ViewUpdated`. Until then every read answers from the current view. Selection, the current cell and an open edit follow their items. Sorting 1 000 000 rows keeps the UI thread busy for about 1 ms instead of the whole sort. A source you create keeps rebuilding synchronously (threshold `int.MaxValue`); the MAUI and Uno grids use 10 000 (Uno in the browser stays synchronous). Values are read on the worker, so accessors, comparers, the filter predicate, group selectors and custom aggregates must be safe to call from another thread while a rebuild runs (see the `BackgroundRebuildThreshold` remarks). `ExpandToItem` completes a pending rebuild synchronously.
- `KumikoStyle.MaxFrozenColumnsWidthRatio` (default two thirds): the largest share of the grid's width the frozen columns keep while the grid scrolls horizontally; beyond it frozen columns are unpinned until they fit (#268, see Fixed).
- `SkiaResourceCache.CreateContext(SKCanvas)` (`KumikoUI.SkiaSharp`): starts a frame on a canvas and returns the cache's reusable `SkiaDrawingContext`, so a host that draws every frame allocates no context object. `new SkiaDrawingContext(canvas, cache)` still works and allocates a small object per frame. Both hosts use `CreateContext` (#251).
- Exact hit regions (#101): `KumikoRenderer.InputController` connects a renderer to the controller it draws for; the renderer then publishes the grouping panel chips it measured while drawing to the controller's hit tester, so a press on a chip or its remove button lands on what is drawn whatever the font (INPUT-12). Both hosts connect their grid's renderer and controller. The header filter icon and a group header's chevron are hit-tested from the same geometry the renderer draws them with (the filter icon moves left of the sort arrow on a sorted column, the chevron moves right of a left drag handle). `KumikoStyle.ColumnResizeGripWidth` (12, mouse and pen) and `KumikoStyle.TouchColumnResizeGripWidth` (32, finger) size the column resize grip by pointer type (INPUT-15); the grip reaches at most a quarter of each neighboring column, so narrow headers keep their middle. `KumikoHitTester.HitTest` has an overload that takes the `KumikoPointerDeviceType`; a finger also gets a wider filter icon and chevron target and grouping chips as tall as the panel.
- Hover and pressed feedback (#101). A mouse or pen hovering a sortable column header, a filter icon, a grouping panel chip or its remove button, a group header (its chevron), a Boolean cell's check box or an enabled action button draws `KumikoStyle.HoverOverlayColor` over it; a press on one, with any pointer, draws `KumikoStyle.PressedOverlayColor` while the pointer stays on it, and drops it once the press becomes a pan or a drag. Both colors are translucent (black on Light, white on Dark, cyan on High Contrast); a transparent color turns that feedback off. Core redraws only when the target under the pointer changes, and the hand cursor shows over exactly the same controls. Custom cell renderers get the pointer through `CellRenderContext.PointerPosition` and `IsPointerPressed`, the paints through `PaintCache.HoverOverlay` and `PressedOverlay`, and report their controls through the new `IInteractiveCellRenderer.GetControlIndexAt` (a default interface method). MAUI now delivers hover from a mouse on Android and from a trackpad or mouse on iPad, as it did on Mac Catalyst and Windows; Uno delivers it on every head.
- Transitions (#101): a tapped group's rows slide open from under its header (or close up under it), a dragged column header lifts with a soft shadow and settles into its slot when dropped (or back, when the drag is canceled), and the current row's highlight fades in, in 120 to 200 ms with an ease-out. They are driven by the hosts' frame loop (`KumikoInputController.UpdateAnimations`, `IsAnimating`) and allocate nothing per frame. `KumikoStyle.EnableAnimations` (default true) turns them off per style; `KumikoInputController.AnimationsEnabled` (default false, for hosts that do not step them) is set by the MAUI and Uno grids unless the platform asks for reduced motion (iOS and Mac Catalyst Reduce Motion, Android animations off, Windows and Uno `UISettings.AnimationsEnabled`).
- Momentum presets (#101): `ScrollSettings.FromPreset(KumikoMomentumPreset)` tunes the inertial scroller's friction, speed cap and stop and fling thresholds for `IOS` (a long `UIScrollView`-like coast), `Android` (shorter, settles sooner) or `Desktop` (a brief coast that needs a deliberate flick); `Default` is the previous defaults. The MAUI grid uses the iOS preset on iPhone and iPad, Android on Android and Desktop on Mac Catalyst and Windows; the Uno grid uses iOS and Android on those heads and Desktop on the others. Assigning `ScrollSettings` replaces the preset; assigning null goes back to it.
- Optional haptics (#101): `KumikoInputController.HapticFeedbackRequested` (`KumikoHapticEventArgs` with a `KumikoHapticKind`) is raised when a finger or pen picks up a row or column header (`DragStart`), drops it (`Drop`), and on a long press that asks for a context menu or edits a cell (`LongPress`); never for a mouse. `KumikoDataGrid.EnableHaptics` on both hosts (default false) answers it with a short vibration: `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator` on iOS, the view's `PerformHapticFeedback` on Android (no permission needed).
- `docs/INTERACTION.md` lists every interaction timing and threshold in one table per area: gestures (double tap, long press, pan, drag and slop distances), touch and mouse target sizes, momentum presets, feedback and transitions, editors and the frame loop (#101).
- The Uno WebAssembly head honors the browser's `prefers-reduced-motion` (no transitions) and uses the Android momentum preset when the browser's main pointer is a finger (`pointer: coarse`), read through a `[JSImport]` of `matchMedia` (#101).
- `KumikoInputController.ActivePopup`: the popup the grid has open on top of its cells (a column's filter popup, for example), or null; read-only, for UI tests and diagnostics. The MAUI sample's DevFlow extension reads it instead of Core internals, and KumikoUI.Core no longer grants `InternalsVisibleTo` to the sample (#112).
- `docs/uno/README.md` is now the Uno user guide (setup per head, usage, render surface, keyboard and input methods, theming, fonts, images, platform notes and known limits); the numbered design notes moved to `docs/uno/plan/` as a historical record (#96).
- Contributor documentation regenerated from the code (#96): `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/RENDERING.md` (real pass order, both hosts' frame loops, background rebuilds), the Copilot instructions and prompts, a new `uno-control.instructions.md`, and the testing instructions. `eng/DocsIdentifiers` fails CI when a backticked type, member or file name in them does not exist in the code.
- Dragging a column header to the edge of a narrow grid scrolls the scrolling columns sideways (edge autoscroll, like the row drag), so a column can be dropped at a position that is off screen. The bands are `ScrollSettings.AutoScrollEdgeSize` wide and sit inside the scrolling pane's left and right edges; the hosts' frame loops already step `UpdateAutoScroll`, and `IsAutoScrolling` now also covers a column drag.
- MAUI on iOS and the Uno heads (iOS, Android, WebAssembly): editing a cell in the bottom rows scrolls it above the on-screen keyboard, with a bottom inset while the keyboard is up so the last rows can be reached; it ends with the edit or the keyboard (#258). Android on MAUI uses the same shared geometry.
- MAUI: `KumikoFonts` (KumikoUI.Maui) registers fonts from the app package with the grid renderer, matching the Uno helper (#75). `RegisterFromAppPackageAsync(family, fileName)` and the overload taking a sequence of `(family, fileName)` pairs open the file with `FileSystem.OpenAppPackageFileAsync` without blocking and never fault for a missing or unreadable font (the grid uses the system font); `RegisterFromStream` registers a stream you opened.
- `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` and the license texts of the sample fonts (Open Sans and Material Icons under Apache-2.0, Noto Sans JP under the SIL OFL 1.1) next to them in `samples/Shared/Fonts` (#75).
- Icon packs (#119): every built-in glyph of the grid and of the drawn components (group chevrons, sort arrows, the filter button, the grouping chips' remove button and separator, the drag grip, check marks, the combo box arrow, the numeric plus and minus, the date picker's calendar, month and time arrows) is drawn by a replaceable `IKumikoIconProvider` (`KumikoUI.Core.Rendering`), set with `KumikoStyle.IconProvider` or, for a component used on its own, `DrawnComponent.IconProvider`. Each slot is a `KumikoIcon` value. `KumikoIconProvider.Default` is the built-in vector set (derive from it to replace a few glyphs); `KumikoFontIconProvider` draws glyphs of an icon font registered with `SkiaFontRegistrar` or `KumikoFonts`, with `CreateMaterialIcons` mapping every icon for Material Icons. The All Components sample page of both hosts switches between the built-in set and Material Icons. See "Icons" in the README.
- Context menus and tap events (#100). `KumikoInputController.ContextRequested` (`KumikoContextRequestedEventArgs`: `Trigger`, `Region`, `RowIndex`, `ColumnIndex`, `Column`, `DataItem`, `X`, `Y`, `DeviceType`, `IsHeader`) is raised by a right click, on its release, and by a long press with a finger or a pen that neither starts a row drag nor edits the cell (`KumikoContextTrigger.SecondaryButton`, `LongPress`). On a data row the row under the point is selected first unless it is already selected, so a menu can act on a multi-selection. `CellTapped` (`KumikoCellTappedEventArgs`, with the column, position and click count) and `HeaderTapped` (`KumikoHeaderTappedEventArgs`, raised after the tap sorted) report primary taps. Both hosts re-surface them as `ContextMenuRequested`, `CellTapped` and `HeaderTapped`, with `ContextMenuRequestedCommand`, `CellTappedCommand` and `HeaderTappedCommand`; the MAUI host reports the secondary click on Mac Catalyst and iPad and a mouse's right button on Android. Both sample apps show a context menu. See "Context menus" in the README.
- `KumikoSource.BeginUpdate()` returns a `KumikoUpdateScope` whose `Dispose` calls `EndUpdate()`, so `using (source.BeginUpdate()) { ... }` ends a batch even when a change throws (#69).
- Saved layouts (#98): `KumikoLayoutState` holds column order, width, visibility and freeze mode, the sort, the column filters and the grouping. Take it with `GetLayoutState()` on the MAUI and Uno grids (or `KumikoLayoutState.Capture(source)`), store it with `ToJson()`, and restore it with `KumikoLayoutState.FromJson(json)` and `ApplyLayoutState(state)` (or `state.ApplyTo(source)`) as one change. The JSON uses System.Text.Json source generation, so it is Native AOT and trimming safe. Columns are matched by the new `KumikoColumn.Key`, else `PropertyName`; saved columns the grid no longer has are ignored, and columns the layout does not mention keep their place. New types: `KumikoColumnLayoutState`, `KumikoGroupLayoutState`, `KumikoFilterLayoutState`, `KumikoFilterConditionLayoutState`, `KumikoFilterValueKind`. See "Saving and restoring the layout" in the README.
- `KumikoSource.SetDisplayIndex(column, displayIndex)` moves a column to an on-screen position within its pane, the counterpart of `GetDisplayIndex` (#98).
- `KumikoSource.ColumnOrderChanged`, raised when `ReorderColumn` (and so a header drag, `SetDisplayIndex` or a layout) changes the order of `Columns` (#98).
- The README documents column reordering: what a drag does, panes, and what `ColumnReordered`'s indices mean (#98).
- Image columns load their values (#63). `Image` cells accept URLs (`http`, `https`, `file`, `data`), file and app package names, `byte[]`, streams and stream factories, MAUI `ImageSource`s (`FileImageSource`, `UriImageSource`, `StreamImageSource`) and, on Uno, `ms-appx:///`/`ms-appdata:///` URIs and `BitmapImage`s, as well as `SKImage`/`SKBitmap` as before. Each grid's new `ImageCache` (`KumikoImageCache`, KumikoUI.SkiaSharp) downloads and decodes images off the UI thread through one shared `HttpClient`, redraws when they are ready, keeps them in a bounded LRU cache (`MaxCount`, `MaxBytes`, `MaxDecodedSize`) that disposes evicted images and cancels their downloads, and is cleared when the grid is unloaded or disconnected. Cache hits allocate nothing in the render loop. New Core hook `IKumikoImageResolver` (`KumikoImageStatus`), set with `KumikoRenderer.ImageResolver` and passed to renderers as `CellRenderContext.ImageResolver`; `IKumikoImageLoader` and `KumikoImageLoader` load other kinds of values. Values nothing can load, and the first failed load of each kind, are reported once through `Trace` instead of drawing an empty cell silently. See "Images" in the README; both samples have an Images page.
- MAUI: `KumikoDataGrid.RenderMode` (`KumikoRenderMode`: `Auto`, `Software`, `Hardware`) and `ActiveRenderMode` (#71). `Hardware` draws on SkiaSharp's `SKGLView` (OpenGL ES on Android and iOS, Metal on Mac Catalyst, ANGLE on Windows), `Software` on `SKCanvasView`; changing it at run time replaces the surface. The MAUI sample's Large Data page has a picker for it.
- Core: `PopupManager.TryGetVisibleBounds(out KumikoRect)` returns the union of the visible popups' bounds without allocating (#71).
- **KumikoUI.Uno** text input goes through the text-input adapter (#43):
  - The hidden text box now holds a copy of the open editor's text and selection instead of a placeholder it reset after every keystroke. Input-method composition (Japanese, Chinese, Korean, dead keys) is passed to the editor as marked text through the text box's composition events and committed when it ends, so composing works on the desktop and in the browser. Suggestions and autocorrect that replace a word replace it in the editor instead of adding characters, and fast typing is no longer delivered twice.
  - A key is marked handled only when the grid used it: Tab and Shift+Tab past the last (first) editable cell, or with no current cell, move focus out of the grid, and Escape with nothing to cancel, or Enter on a cell that does nothing with it, reaches the page.
  - The hidden text box is no longer hit-testable, announced by screen readers or 64×32 at the grid's center, focusing it no longer scrolls a page that hosts the grid, and it no longer makes iOS Safari zoom the page (WebAssembly).
  - The grid no longer sets `IsTabStop` on every load or `TabIndex` to 0, so it takes its place in the page's tab order and an app's `IsTabStop="False"` is kept. **Behavior change** for pages that relied on the grid being first in tab order.
  - After a touch edit the keyboard focus stays in the grid and the soft keyboard is hidden, so a hardware keyboard on a tablet keeps navigating the grid.
- `SampleApp.Maui` hosts the [.NET MAUI DevFlow](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/maui/developer-tools/devflow/) agent in Debug builds (never in Release or in the packages), with a `com.kumikoui.sample` agent extension that reports the canvas-drawn grid's state and cell geometry, and `eng/devflow/verify.sh` drives the sample page by page through the `maui devflow` CLI on Mac Catalyst and the iOS Simulator: sorting, filtering, grouping, selection, editing, column resize and reorder, frozen panes, summaries and themes, with a screenshot per step. See [eng/devflow/README.md](eng/devflow/README.md). (#262)
- MAUI on iOS and Mac Catalyst is a native text-input client (#40). The grid's responder implements `UITextInput` and drives the open editor's `ITextInputSession`: Japanese, Chinese and Korean input methods compose marked text in the cell, with their candidate window placed at the text, and commit it; the emoji keyboard, dictation and suggestion-bar words insert whole (a surrogate pair or emoji sequence is never split), also when they open the editor. A numeric editor gets the numbers keyboard; autocorrection, smart quotes and inline predictions are off. Hardware navigation keys (arrows, Tab, Escape, Return, F2, Home, End, Page Up/Down) and Cmd+A/C/X/V/Z/Shift+Z still go to the grid, except while an input method is composing. The hidden `Entry` keyboard proxy is gone on these platforms.
- `DrawnTextBox.GetTextRangeBounds(KumikoTextRange)` and `GetTextIndexAt(float)`: where a range of the text is drawn and which index is at an x position, for a host's text-input adapter (#40).
- MAUI on Android: a native text-input adapter (#41) replaces the hidden `Entry`.
  - The grid's own input view gives the input method an `InputConnection` onto `ITextInputSession`. Composition (Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Gboard suggestions), voice input and swipe input reach the editor whole instead of being reset mid-word.
  - Surrounding-text deletion works by grapheme cluster, so an emoji is never split.
  - The soft keyboard type follows the editor: number keys for numeric columns (with a decimal key unless the cell holds an integer), and no suggestions in the filter search box.
  - A hardware keyboard now navigates the grid: arrows, Tab and Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape, F2, Home and End, Page Up and Page Down, Delete, Ctrl/Meta+A/C/V/X/Z/Y, and dead keys.
  - The edited cell is kept above the soft keyboard. See "Android" in [docs/TEXT-INPUT.md](docs/TEXT-INPUT.md#android) for the `WindowSoftInputMode` guidance.
- **KumikoUI.Maui** on Windows: full keyboard support and a text-input adapter (#42). The grid's platform view takes the keyboard focus and sends every key in the README's keyboard table to the grid (arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down, Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape, F2, Delete, Backspace, Space, Ctrl+A/C/X/V/Z/Y) with its modifiers; navigation keys no longer move focus or scroll the page, and Tab past the last tab stop still moves focus on. While a text editor is open, the Windows text services (`CoreTextEditContext`) are attached to it, so input methods compose in place with the candidate window at the edited cell, where Windows offers them to desktop apps; otherwise characters, surrogate pairs and text committed by an input method's own window arrive through `CharacterReceived`. Ctrl+Alt (AltGr) types characters instead of triggering shortcuts.

### Changed
- The KumikoUI packages depend on each other at their exact version (`[1.0.0]` rather than `>= 1.0.0`): the hosts use KumikoUI.Core internals, so a mismatched set now fails at restore instead of at run time (#112, decision D3).
- The documentation snippet check also compiles the C# and XAML blocks of the NuGet READMEs (`docs/nuget/*.md`) against both hosts (#236). `eng/DocsSnippets` splits statements followed by type declarations, infers the host from the code or the package README, and pairs a `partial` page class with its XAML page, so the NuGet READMEs need no annotations.
- The MAUI and Uno samples share one `samples/Shared/Fonts` folder instead of keeping two copies of the fonts, and the MAUI sample registers its fonts through `KumikoFonts` instead of private blocking code (#75).
- The built-in glyphs are drawn by the new icon provider and look slightly different: the active filter button is a solid funnel instead of an outline with a dot, the grouping chip and filter popup sort arrows have the header arrow's proportions, the numeric editor's plus and minus are filled shapes, and the date picker's time arrows point up above the value and down below it (they pointed toward it).
- **Behavior change:** only the primary mouse button (or a finger) selects, sorts, scrolls, drags and edits (#100). A right click no longer sorts a header, toggles a group, starts a column or row drag or resize, toggles a Boolean cell or opens an editor; a middle click does nothing and is left to the page. A touch or pen long press that used to only move the current cell now selects the row and raises `ContextRequested`, and lifting the finger afterwards does not tap. A mouse held down is unchanged.
- **Breaking:** `KumikoSource` is UI-thread-only (#69). It belongs to the thread that last called `SetItems` or `Attach` (the thread that assigned `ItemsSource`, in a grid). A collection change, an item `PropertyChanged` or a `KumikoSource` call from any other thread now throws `InvalidOperationException` before the view is touched (it used to rebuild the view on that thread while the UI thread drew from it); the source then re-reads the collection on its own thread through the `SynchronizationContext` captured at `SetItems`/`Attach`, or on the next `Refresh()`. Code running under that context counts as the UI thread. Post background changes to the UI thread (`MainThread.BeginInvokeOnMainThread`, `DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue`, `SynchronizationContext.Post`); see "Threading" in the README.
- **Breaking:** `KumikoSource.BeginUpdate()` returns `KumikoUpdateScope` instead of `void` (source compatible; recompile). Inside a batch, a collection change that needs a rebuild (an active sort, grouping or summary, a reset or replace) no longer rebuilds the view per change: the view is rebuilt once, at `EndUpdate` or at the first row read before it, so a loop of `Add`s under a sort costs one sort (#69).
- **Breaking:** a `PropertyChanged` of a property that only table summaries use no longer rebuilds the view and now raises `ViewChanged` as `Redraw` instead of `Rebuild` (#69). Sum, Average and Count follow the change from the item's old and new value in constant time; Min, Max and Custom are recomputed over the visible rows without re-filtering, re-sorting or regrouping (once per batch). 100 such changes on 100,000 rows with a Sum summary take about 3–5 ms in total on the calling thread (24 µs once warm), where each one used to rebuild the whole view. A group key, group summary or caption summary property still rebuilds while grouping is active. A `double` total updated in place may differ from a fresh sum in the last bits; `Refresh()` recomputes it.
- **Behavior change:** a `PropertyChanged` of a property that only group summaries or the caption summary aggregate with Sum, Average or Count no longer rebuilds the grouped view; the groups containing the item update in place and `ViewChanged` is a `Redraw` (#254). Min, Max and Custom group aggregates still rebuild.
- Grouping partitions one shared index buffer instead of a `List<int>` per group, formats a group's display text once instead of per row, and composes `GroupHeaderInfo.GroupPath` on first read instead of a path string per group per rebuild; sorting reads each sort value once per row instead of twice per comparison (#254).
- Summaries are computed in a single pass per property with streaming aggregates instead of a list of boxed values per summary column; group summary rows of one group share the pass (#69).
- A condition filter no longer formats every row's display text; only a value-list (`SelectedValues`) filter does. A numeric filter over 100K rows allocates 2.4 MB instead of 5.3 MB (#69).
- Grouped views store their rows as structs in a reused list instead of one object per row: grouping 100K rows with summaries allocates 9–10.5 MB instead of 17.5–18.8 MB and is faster (#69).
- **Behavior change:** a user's column drag now moves the column in the grid's `Columns` collection as well as in `DataSource.Columns`, so the collection keeps the on-screen order and adding a column, or returning to the page, no longer undoes the drag (#98). The grids' `ColumnReordered` event is raised by the grid (the sender) after the column moved, whatever the order handlers were added in; it used to forward `InputController.ColumnReordered` and could run before the move.
- MAUI: **Behavior change** — `RenderMode` defaults to `Auto`, which rasterizes on the GPU on Android and Mac Catalyst; iOS (OpenGL ES, deprecated by Apple) and Windows stay on `SKCanvasView` unless `Hardware` is set. Set `RenderMode="Software"` to keep the previous surface everywhere. On Android the GPU view paints on its own GL thread, so the grid records each frame into an `SKPicture` on the UI thread and the GL thread plays it back. (#71)
- MAUI: the 16 ms dispatcher timer is replaced by the platform's frame callback (`CADisplayLink` on iOS and Mac Catalyst, up to 120 Hz; `Choreographer` on Android; `CompositionTarget.Rendering` on Windows), which runs only while a fling, edge autoscroll or editor animation is in progress and stops on the first idle frame. Redraw requests are coalesced to one paint per frame where an invalidation paints synchronously (Windows, the Android GPU surface). (#71)
- MAUI: the caret blink redraws only at blink transitions, in phase with the caret, and on the software surface it copies the last full frame back and rasterizes only the editor and popup area. Neither SkiaSharp view can invalidate a sub-rectangle, so the GPU surfaces still redraw the whole frame on a blink. (#71)
- Core: `InertialScroller.Update` integrates the decaying velocity over the frame interval, so a fling travels the same distance at 60, 120 Hz or with uneven frames. A 16 ms step is unchanged; a longer step travels slightly less than before (it no longer moves at the starting speed for the whole step). (#71)

...

The full release notes are longer than NuGet allows: https://github.com/TheEightBot/KumikoUI/releases/tag/v1.0.0-preview.1
